metadata.theme: Courage, noticing small details, and asking for help
metadata.premise: When thick fog swallows the harbour, young lamp keeper Fen must find out why the old lighthouse lamp went dark before the fishing boats come home.

items.name: Soft cloth
items.description: A soft cloth from the old chest. It is made for wiping the brass mirror.

clues.name: Damp mirror
clues.description: Fog leaves a wet film on the brass mirror. A dim mirror makes a dim lamp.

passages.title: The Fog Rolls In
paragraphs: Fen stood on the path by the old lighthouse. The fog was thick and grey.
The lamp at the top was dark. Out at sea, every ship and fishing boat needed that light.
Pip the gull hopped onto a bench. She tapped a shell with her beak, tap, tap, tap.
Fen felt a bit afraid. But Fen wanted to help much more.

choices.label: Look in the shed for a lamp tool
Sit on the bench and ask Gran Tull

passages.title: The Garden Shed
paragraphs: The shed door was shut. Fen lifted the chain and pushed.
The door creaked wide. Inside, fish nets hung from the wall.
An old chest sat under the shelf. A dry shell lay on the lid.

passages.title: Inside the Chest
paragraphs: Fen lifted the lid of the chest. A grey moth fluttered out and zipped away.
Under the lid lay a soft cloth, folded flat. It smelled of lamp oil and brass.
Fen tucked the cloth in a pocket. It might help with the lamp.

choices.label: Take the cloth to the tower

passages.title: Gran Tull on the Bench
paragraphs: Gran Tull sat on the bench in a thick wool coat. She had kept the lamp for many years.
"The lamp is not broken, Fen," she said. "Look at the glass, not the flame."
Fen did not know what she meant. Fen asked her to tell more.

choices.label: Ask Gran Tull what the glass can tell you

passages.title: A Small Detail
paragraphs: "Fog is wet air," said Gran Tull. "It leaves a film on the brass mirror."
"A mist on the mirror makes the light dim. A wipe will fix it, and much faster than you think."
Fen smiled. Asking for help had been the right thing to do.
A moth tapped on the window. Pip chased it down the path.

choices.label: Go to the foot of the tower

passages.title: The Foot of the Tower
paragraphs: Fen stood at the tower door. The fog was so thick that the shed was hard to see.
Pip sat on the step. Far off, a ship horn gave a low, sad call.
Fen thought about the path ahead. Was there more to find first?

choices.label: Go back to the shed and the chest
Go back to the bench and Gran Tull
Climb the stairs to the lamp room

passages.title: The Lamp Room Door
paragraphs: At the top of the stairs, Fen pushed the lamp room door. It was not shut tight.
The brass mirror stood dull and misty. The wick sat cold in its dish.
Down in the bay, a ship horn called again. Time was short.

choices.label: Wipe the mirror with the soft cloth
choices.lockedHint: You need a soft cloth and a clue about the mirror.

choices.label: Run down the path with a small lantern

passages.title: The Dark Lamp
paragraphs: Fen rubbed the brass mirror with the cloth. The mist wiped away, and the brass shone.
Then Fen lit the wick. A small gold flame woke up and danced.
The mirror caught the flame. A bright beam shot out into the thick fog.
But the beam must sweep the whole bay. Fen could turn the mirror alone, or call Gran Tull.

choices.label: Turn the mirror with the cloth and sweep the bay
choices.lockedHint: Fen needs the cloth and the mirror clue to turn it well.

choices.label: Call Gran Tull to help turn the mirror

passages.title: The Bay Shines
paragraphs: Fen turned the clean mirror, slow and steady. The beam swept across the bay.
One by one, the boats saw the light. Each ship turned toward the harbour.
Soon the dock rang with happy shouts and the smell of fresh fish.
Gran Tull came up the stairs and gave Fen a shell from her coat. "You noticed the small thing," she said.

passages.title: Two Pairs of Hands
paragraphs: Gran Tull climbed the stairs, slow but sure. She put a hand on the chain that turns the mirror.
Together they swept the beam across the bay. It took much longer, and the cloth got damp.
The boats came home late, with their fish and a few sleepy shouts.
Fen sat on the step with Pip. Asking for help had been brave, too.

passages.title: A Small Light
paragraphs: Fen ran down the path with a small lantern. The fog hid the light after ten steps.
On the dock, Fen waved and waved. A ship horn answered, but no boat came in.
Gran Tull wrapped a thick coat around Fen. "Brave try," she said. "The lamp room has the answer."
Fen looked up at the dark tower. Next time, Fen would look at the glass first.
